speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the swelling and pain in your right ring finger: when did it start, is it constant or intermittent, and have you noticed any redness, warmth, or joint deformity?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a traumatic injury. Can you describe exactly what the finger looks like now—specifically, is there visible deformity, a lump, or any discoloration compared to your other hand? Please also tell me if you were able to fully bend or straighten the finger after the injury.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Lag of the DIP Joint). The history of forced flexion while the finger was extended, combined with the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and the finger resting in an extended position, is classic for an avulsion fracture of the distal phalanx base or a ruptured extensor tendon.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP and Lateral views) to rule out a bony avulsion fragment.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
